machatzit-hashekel/12:_: (12) That they do not fly etc. — therefore it appears to me that Rosh in his responsum (who holds we require specifically that they fly outside the boundary) follows his reason, meaning as Magen Avraham wrote in the seif katan before this that Rosh holds like reason one that depends on coming to the coop and their sustenance upon you, and because of trapping he does not require sustenance upon you and it suffices that they come to the coop; rather they must be designated and not muktzeh, therefore we require specifically that they fly outside the boundary, for even though they fly and thereby their sustenance is not upon him — what of it, since they come to the coop in the evening they are trapped, but he requires sustenance upon them so they are designated and not muktzeh; and therefore we require specifically that they fly outside the boundary, for since they do not fly outside the boundary they are still designated and not muktzeh, as we say regarding wild animals in siman 498 seif 3; but in his rulings he retracted and holds that even so the reason is because of trapping, meaning even if they come to the coop, if their sustenance is not upon him it is called lacking trapping, for otherwise designation would help for them, and why do we rule that designation does not help for them since their sustenance is not upon him — rather that they be designated and not forbidden because of muktzeh; if so sustenance upon him is required, for otherwise they lack trapping; therefore even if they fly within the boundary, since through this their sustenance is not upon him, even though they are designated as stated, nevertheless they are forbidden because of lacking trapping — such is Magen Avraham's apparent intention; but his words require further study, for behold the essence of the Gemara's words is thus stated: on that which Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said whatever requires trapping is forbidden — we say how is trapping defined? R' Yosef said R' Yehuda said: whatever we say "bring the trap and we will trap"; Abaye said to him: but geese and chickens — we say "bring the trap" etc., and it is taught: one who traps geese and chickens is exempt; Rabbah bar R' Huna said R' Yehuda said: these come to the coop in the evening etc., and behold dovecote pigeons and upper pigeons that come to the coop in the evening — and it is taught: one who traps dovecote pigeons and upper pigeons is liable; rather Rabbah bar R' Huna said R' Yehuda said: these come to the coop and their sustenance is upon you etc.; Rav Mari said these are frequent etc. — end of the Gemara; and if so to establish Rabbah bar R' Huna's words: the reason the baraita teaches dovecote pigeons and upper pigeons — one who traps is liable — deals with coming to the coop in the evening; rather since their sustenance is not upon you he is liable, for per Mishna Berurah's responsum to Rosh who does not require sustenance upon them but only that they be designated and not muktzeh — if so why is one liable for dovecote and upper pigeons since they come to the coop and are not lacking trapping; they are that sustenance is not upon them and they are not designated — why should he be liable because of muktzeh prohibition? Perhaps one can say, and so is Rashi's language there: and their sustenance upon you — therefore they are like an animal and are considered designated — end of his words; behold Rashi also wrote that through sustenance upon him they are considered designated; and what difference to me whether because of prohibition of designation or because of liability — we deal with whether trapping applies, not with designation; if so one must say: even though through coming to the coop they are trapped, nevertheless if their sustenance is not upon them, since they are not designated, his mind is not upon them and it is as though they are not in his domain; and through this it is called lacking trapping and through this he is liable because of trapping — and so is the view of Rosh's responsum; therefore if they do not fly outside the boundary, behold sustenance is upon him, nevertheless they are like designated and as though in his domain and are not lacking trapping; not so when they fly outside the boundary it is as though they are not in his domain; but Rosh in his rulings holds even if his mind is upon them, all that their sustenance is not upon him — namely they do not fly outside the boundary — nevertheless they lack trapping, for otherwise designation would help for them even if they fly outside the boundary; and nevertheless designation does not help for them since their sustenance is not upon him; rather they must be designated and not forbidden as muktzeh; if so prohibition of trapping caused it, since sustenance is not upon him — designation would help for them even if they fly outside the boundary; and nevertheless it is difficult.

And see Avodat HaGashmi there in siman 499; and Bach challenged: since R' Eliezer establishes the latter clause with tied ones, if so the first clause too "he left two and found three" also deals with tied ones; and if so it should be difficult in any case — if he found two tied and the third not tied, why are the two forbidden — behold we know that the untied one came from elsewhere and the two tied ones are what he designated; and if he found all three tied, if so it is obvious they are forbidden, for it is seen that all three are what he did not designate; and if he found them all untied, why specifically "left two and found three" — even if he found only two untied they are forbidden, for in any case they are others since he designated tied ones; and the words that in truth even if he found two they are forbidden since they are untied, and it mentioned "found three" because it deals with all cases, whether he designated tied or untied, and when he designated untied it is forbidden only when he found three — therefore it mentioned "found three." mechaber/1:main: Laws of preparation on Yom Tov. 17 sections: One may not trap fish from fish pools. {Rama: Even in a place where they do not require trapping, since the pool is very wide and the fish slip away in all directions. (HaMagid ch. 2)}
mechaber/2:main: Fish, fowl, and animals that are muktzeh — one may not water them on Yom Tov and may not place food before them, lest one come to take from them. And anything that is forbidden to eat or use because it is muktzeh is forbidden to handle.
mechaber/3:main: Even doubtful trapping is forbidden — for example, traps for animals, fish, and fowl that were spread out before Yom Tov, and the next day one finds things in them — they are forbidden unless it is known that they were trapped while it was still day. If the traps are found damaged from before Yom Tov, it is evident that they were trapped before Yom Tov.
mechaber/4:main: A doubtful case of muktzeh is permitted on the second day of Yom Tov, since it is a double doubt.
mechaber/5:main: If one blocked a water channel at its entrance and exit before Yom Tov, one may take fish from it on Yom Tov, since they are considered already trapped (given that the channel is narrow and they cannot slip away). (HaMagid ch. 8)
mechaber/6:main: Geese, chickens, and doves that are in the house or courtyard and are designated for eating — one may trap them and they do not require prior designation.
mechaber/7:main: All other animals and fowl that require trapping — meaning one would have to say "bring a trap and we will catch it" — it is forbidden to trap them or to place food before them. Whatever does not require trapping, one may trap and place food before them.
mechaber/8:main: A deer or gazelle that nested in an orchard and gave birth to fawns there, and they are still small and do not require trapping — they are permitted without prior designation, but only in an orchard adjacent to the city within seventy cubits, since one's attention is upon them. The mother, however, cannot be helped even by designation, since she requires trapping.
mechaber/9:main: Doves of a dovecote, doves of an upper story, and birds that nested in clay vessels built into walls for birds to nest in — it is forbidden to trap them, and therefore designation does not help for them. This applies to adult birds, but small ones that cannot yet fly may be trapped, though they do require designation.
mechaber/10:main: How is designation done? One says "this one and that one I will take tomorrow" — one need not shake them. But saying "from here I will take tomorrow" is not sufficient.
mechaber/11:main: If one designated the entire dovecote but only needs a pair, it is not effective. {Rama: But if it is possible he will need the entire dovecote, he may designate the whole dovecote and take what he needs the next day. (Rabbeinu Yerucham and Hagahot Asheiri, ch. 1 of Beitzah)}
mechaber/12:main: If one designated two and found three, or designated black ones and white ones in nests separated by a partition and found the black ones in place of the white ones and the white ones in place of the black ones — they are forbidden unless he recognizes them.
mechaber/13:main: If one designated three and found two, they are permitted. {Rama: (And even if they were tied together, one separates them from each other.} (Beit Yosef)}
mechaber/14:main: If one designated birds inside the nest and found them in front of the nest, they are forbidden. If there is no other nest nearby, they are permitted. This applies when they are hopping, but if they can fly they are forbidden. And even if there is another nest within fifty cubits, if it is around a corner such that one cannot see it from this nest — since they are only hopping and not flying, wherever it hops and does not return, it is evident it belongs to that nest and has not hopped away from it. {Rama: (If one designated birds inside the nest and found them at the entrance of the nest, they are permitted.} (Or Zarua)}
mechaber/15:main: If a non-Jew brought a Jew a gift on Yom Tov of young doves from dovecotes he owns in the city — since they do not require trapping, they are permitted.
mechaber/16:main: One who slaughters an animal on Yom Tov — it is better that he not inspect it until after he skins it, because if it is found to be a tereifah he will not be permitted to skin it.
mechaber/17:main: If it is found to be a tereifah, it is forbidden to handle it, but one may sell it to a non-Jew in the same manner as selling to a Jew was permitted — without weighing it and without mentioning a specific sum of money. If he does not trust him, he may take a pledge from him.

turei-zahav/1:א: (א) One does not trap etc. I will set forth briefly the Gemara needed for this and the view of the authorities who said in the mishnah Eruvin one does not trap fish from ponds on Yom Tov (Rashi explained because it was possible to trap from yesterday and leave them in a trap in the water and tomorrow retrieve it; and Tosafos gave the reason that trapping is like harvesting, but there is no distinction in ochel nefesh if it was possible from yesterday) — but one traps animals and birds from ponds (Rashi explained that a fish pond is pools of water and an animal pond is enclosures surrounded by a fence and they gather wild animals into them and they bear and raise there) — Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says not all ponds are equal — this is the principle: whatever requires trapping (that one must trap it) is forbidden, and whatever does not require trapping is permitted; and the halacha is like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel; and we establish that which is permitted for animals and birds — namely in small ponds specifically; and we explain in the Gemara that "requires trapping" which Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel mentioned means whatever we say "bring the trap and we will trap" (meaning one must seek stratagems to catch it); and it is stated afterward in the Gemara: Rav said a water channel that he blocked (so fish from outside do not enter from evening, and these he prepared and designated through this act) — they are permitted. And behold Rambam holds Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel refers also to fish; therefore he ruled in ch. 2 of Yom Tov: fish in large ponds and likewise animals and birds in large ponds — whatever requires trapping etc. — this is muktzeh and one does not trap them on Yom Tov; and Ra'avad wrote on this: this is incorrect, for animals and birds that they permitted is only in small ponds, and nevertheless fish are not; and the reason is because they are covered in water from the eye — end of his words; and the fifth Maggid explained Rambam holds Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel refers also to fish and there too it depends on requiring trapping; and Ra'avad and Rashba hold Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel refers only to animals and birds; and Rambam relied on that which we permit in blocking the water channel as written in this siman — and what is the difference between this and a small pond: if in a small pond that does not require trapping its fish are forbidden, why are these permitted? Rather certainly whatever does not require trapping is permitted; and a water channel even if very long, since it is not very wide, the fish within are considered trapped; and the same law applies in small ponds — end of his words; and if so certainly it is difficult on Ra'avad and Rashba from blocking the water channel as the fifth Maggid wrote — support from this for Rambam; and the words of Beit Yosef: and so in ponds it is different for they are very wide, and even though no trap is needed to trap the fish, nevertheless because they are covered from the eye they slip here and there and therefore are not considered trapped; but a water channel, since it is not wide it cannot slip — therefore it is considered trapped — end of his words; and I cannot reconcile at all Beit Yosef's words here, for since according to Ra'avad animals and birds are permitted when not requiring trapping — automatically fish are forbidden even when not requiring trapping, even though they are considered trapped — nevertheless forbidden because they are covered from the eye; if so what helps blocking the water even though it is narrow and does not require trapping — nevertheless it would be forbidden because of covering the water, and it would not help that they are trapped and standing; and there is no place to distinguish between them; and it appears to me to answer the fifth Maggid's question on Ra'avad and Rashba thus: when trapping is required it is forbidden because of muktzeh as written nearby in the name of Rambam; and even though in ch. 1 of Yom Tov Rambam wrote that on Yom Tov is stricter than Shabbat, for muktzeh on Shabbat is permitted and on Yom Tov forbidden, and Ra'avad disagrees and equates Yom Tov to Shabbat — nevertheless it is obvious that in such muktzeh even on Shabbat it is forbidden and even R' Shimon agrees; and this is the reason Ra'avad wrote "because they are covered from the eye" — it is difficult at first glance: is covering from the eye what permits the prohibition of trapping? Behold there is already no trapping since no trap is needed; rather certainly he speaks because of muktzeh; except that for Rambam muktzeh is specifically because of lacking trapping, and for Ra'avad muktzeh is specifically because of covering from the eye; and if so according to both, blocking the water channel is permitted, for the essence of muktzeh reason is since from yesterday he designated his mind away from it and did not prepare it; and this that he blocked from yesterday the water channel — certainly there is no muktzeh here. And this is explained from Rashi's words we mentioned who wrote "and these he prepared" and from outside they will not enter — behold literally as stated; and this is also proven from Rav's words who said a water channel that he blocked on erev Yom Tov, and did not say briefly "a water channel that is blocked is permitted," rather it is clear a person must do an act on erev Yom Tov or before it and remove from muktzeh; and this is very correct in my humble opinion; and Tur's words imply he holds like Ra'avad, for he wrote regarding fish plainly to forbid, except that plain water permits; and for animals and birds he distinguishes between requiring trapping or not — rather certainly forbidden regarding fish even when not requiring trapping because of muktzeh like Ra'avad we mentioned; and so Rashal in chapter Eruvin ruled like Ra'avad and Rashba; and in my humble opinion there is full permission regarding fish that one prepares from erev Yom Tov and puts them into a large perforated box in water, since all do not require trapping and there is no muktzeh among them — it is literally like blocking the water channel we mentioned; and Rashal there in chapter Eruvin also wrote to permit in this box even if a small trap is needed to reach there — there is no trapping on this; except he wrote on this that it appeared to him to distinguish specifically if he wants to take all and cook them it is permitted, but if he wants to take one or two it is forbidden unless he ties from beforehand with a string, for it is no better than dovecote pigeons and upper pigeons that even if they do not fly are forbidden, and the reason lest they be weak and he leave them and move in vain as stated in this siman; and afterward he rejected this and said that there regarding pigeons there is concern lest he move muktzeh, but here where he took them by hand and put them in the box on erev Yom Tov there is no muktzeh at all, for all are fit for him even without designation — thus; and I wondered why he needed to elaborate — it is obvious that it is permitted to take whatever he wishes, like blocking the water channel we mentioned; and further why was it not difficult to him on the mishnah that one traps animals and birds from ponds and we are not concerned lest they not please him and he move in vain — rather certainly only regarding pigeons is there muktzeh prohibition and the essence of permission is through designation — therefore he must designate properly as written in this siman, which is not so with these that do not require designation and there is no muktzeh since they are in small ponds; and similarly regarding fish if he blocks the water channel from yesterday it is as though he takes each fish individually on erev Yom Tov and leaves it there, and tying a string is not needed in my humble opinion; and see in this siman from this: again I saw my honored teacher may he rest in Eden also followed Beit Yosef's distinction according to Ra'avad and Rashba regarding the water channel, and concluded on this that since the container is somewhat wide the fish are forbidden because of trapping according to Ra'avad and Rashba; and so it appears from Rashi's words who found permission in a pond for fish only to trap them from beforehand and leave them in his trap; and I would say regarding the water channel that it is not wide, and whatever is wider than six handbreadths in the measure of the water channel the fish are forbidden — thus. And it appears to me they did not insist the water channel be short, rather since it is long — if it were wide the fish could slip along the length which is very great, not so in a box that is square — even if it slips somewhat from its place it has no place to escape; and the principle they gave here: whatever we do not say "bring the trap" — Rashi explained one will need stratagems to trap it, meaning he spreads food there or spreads it across from end to end; not so when reaching with a trap to the box to take it — even reaching several times until he removes it from there — there is no concern in this, in my humble opinion.
